text.p: These are the highlights of main stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Macedonian government to review a number of draft laws at its regular session. Parliament to return from summer break on August 20. New session planned for August 24 at which the interior ministry's report on the events in Tetovo and Gostivar will be discussed.

- Macedonian customs officials from the region of Radika watchtower, bordering Albania, seized 15 automatic guns, 31 flak jackets and 1,703 bullets from a group of ten Albanians trying to enter Macedonia illegally. Customs officials warned the group to stop, after which it dropped the weapons and fled in the direction of Albania.

- "The confidence of the Macedonian citizens in the system's institutions must be restored and this will positively reflect on Macedonian immigrants who have money and are willing to invest in their country," said Vladimir Ralev, prominent Macedonian businessman.

- A total of 203 million German marks have been collected so far from privatisation in Macedonia, of which 164 million from the sell-off of companies. During the first several months of the year, an inflow of 36 millon marks registered in the Privatisation Agency.
